title: Supreme Court forms panel to examine use of force by police in Delhi's July 20 protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Thursday constituted a five-member high-powered committee headed by its former judge R Subhash Reddy to conduct an independent inquiry into allegations of excessive and disproportionate use of force by police and security personnel during the July 20 student protests. The panel will also examine claims of violence by protesters against police personnel and damage to public property.

Adding to this, The CJP's protest march to Parliament on July 20 amid the agitation over NEET paper leak saw lathi-charge and the alleged use of pellet guns. (RAJ K RAJ / Hindustan Times) A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana shared the competing allegations made out a prima facie case for an independent and impartial investigation.

Meanwhile, The committee comprises justice (retd) R Subhash Reddy, former Supreme Court judge, as chairperson; justice (retd) Ravi Shankar Jha, former Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court; justice (retd) Shalinder Kaur, former Delhi High Court judge; Rishi Kumar Shukla, former CBI director; and L R Bishnoi, retired director general of police, Meghalaya.
Notably, The court shared the composition took into account the members' expertise and experience, as well as the need for diversity on the panel.

As per the latest buzz, The committee has been given a wide-ranging mandate. It will examine allegations that police and other security agencies used pellet guns, electric batons, lathi charges and tear gas without adequate warning or proportionality, causing grievous and lasting injuries to protesters.

In further updates, It will also examine whether police responses during protests and public gatherings were proportionate and adequately balanced the maintenance of public order with the constitutional right to peaceful dissent.

On top of that, Significantly, the committee will consider whether the use of metallic kinetic projectiles or pellets fired from pump-action or projectile-action guns should be banned, given the grave and sometimes irreversible injuries allegedly caused by their deployment against protesters.

The panel will further examine whether police and security personnel should be required to wear proper uniforms and visible nameplates while making arrests or using force during crowd-control operations, to ensure that individual officers can be identified and held accountable.

Adding to this, This movie would've marked Bhagyashri Borse's debut in Bollywood as a lead if the rumours were true. Bhagyashri Borse not in Milap Zaveri’s next, says T-Series Of late, a Filmfare report claimed that Bhagyashri has been finalised as the female lead in Milap’s next with Aditya. However, the production house clarifies that she is not associated with the movie. Putting an end to the ongoing casting buzz, a T-Series spokesperson shared in a note, “The reports of Bhagyashri Borse being a part of T-Series and Milap Zaveri’s soon-to-release project with Aditya Roy Kapur are untrue. The production house will officially announce the star soon.” Details about the movie by T-Series, Milap and Aditya are being closely guarded even as it draws attention. The production house has yet to reveal who has been cast opposite Aditya.

Meanwhile, In July, Milap verified to PTI that his next with Aditya will be an ‘intense and violent’ love story. “I feel maybe I've found my forte with romance. Earlier, Marjaavaan succeeded in a big way; Ek Deewane Ki Deewaniyat was a smash hit,” he shared, adding, “So, romance is a key integral part of my stories, and I think going forward it will remain along with action. So, romance, action, dialogue baazi, these are things I like to do as a director-writer and till audiences like my films, I'll try to keep doing them.” He did not reveal further details about the movie at that time.

Notably, Bhagyashri featured in cameos in the 2023 Hindi movie Yaariyan 2 and the 2024 movie Chandu Champion. Had the rumour turned out to be true, it would’ve been her debut as a lead star in Bollywood. However, the star has since found fame in the south. Despite the criticism, director Harish Shankar and star Ravi Teja received for Mr Bachchan, Bhagyashri’s debut did not go unnoticed.

As per the latest buzz, In 2025, Bhagyashri impressed followers with her performances in Kingdom and Andhra King Taluka. But it was her role in the Tamil movie Kaantha , which saw Dulquer Salmaan, Samuthirakani and Rana Daggubati as her co-stars, that left many impressed. This year, she shared the screen with Akhil Akkineni in his comeback movie, Lenin . She now has Seyon with Sivakarthikeyan in Tamil lined up. The movie is produced by Kamal Haasan.

title: 'Why not Jannat': Emraan Hashmi was not sold on Awarapan 2, reveals Visheh Bhatt, softened after re-releases worked
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The success of Awarapan 2 almost seems like a foregone conclusion at this point. The first movie, rolled out in 2007, is a cult classic with a dedicated and loyal fan base. The sequel, rolled out last week, is already Emraan Hashmi ’s highest-grossing movie. But hindsight is always 20/20, as they say. When the movie was in the ideation stage, Emraan was not very confident about it, reveals producer Vishesh Bhatt . In an exclusive chat with Hindustan Times, the filmmaker talks about how the much-anticipated sequel came to be.

Adding to this, Vishesh Bhatt and Emraan Hashmi after the rollout of Awarapan 2. ‘Awarapan 2 was an emotional decision’ Ask him if making Awarapan 2 was a creative decision or a business decision, and Vishesh promptly says, “It was an emotional decision.” The filmmaker elaborates, “I think we followed a lot of things emotionally, which probably converted. That's why the audience feels that way. Creative came from the emotional, and then comes the business.”

Meanwhile, The original Awarapan, rolled out in 2007, was a massive box-office failure. It later attained cult status, but the box-office blemish remained. Shivam, the character played by Emraan Hashmi, gained a fan following too. Talking about bringing Emraan back, Vishesh says, “There were so many layers and so much depth in that character that we had to bring him. He is a broken man, and we have all taken his pain for 18-19 years.”
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Vishesh Films (@visheshfilms)

As per the latest buzz, Vishesh Films has a good track record with sequels. Its top 5 grossing films are all sequels. They pioneered the ‘spiritual successor’ trend in Hindi cinema with thematically connected franchises like Raaz, Aashiqui, and Jism. But with Awarapan, Vishesh decided to bring back Shivam and continue the same story. “People would ask, ‘You have so many franchises. Why Awarapan 19 years later?',” he recalls.

In further updates, “I shared it actually came from feeling a lack of emotions connecting to the audience in me during Covid. Those 2-3 years, there was a lot of at-home watching, and a lot of things were being made for that. But I felt that when the cinemas open, what would I want to go and see? I felt drama was missing. Everything is being mounted with VFX and grand scale. We have done the same things here, but to support the drama. Everything looked like a very clever cover-up for lack of drama.”

On top of that, Vishesh reveals that even Emraan was not fully sold on the idea of an Awarapan sequel when he first approached him a few years ago. “Jannat came just after Awarapan, and a lot of learnings from why Awarapan didn't work went into Jannat. And that was a success. Emraan shared Awarapan is a beautiful movie, but our hearts did break when it didn't do well. So, why not Jannat? That is close to you, and it worked. It's almost obvious to me, forget the market, that we would take that forward. But, I shared I am stuck on Awarapan,” he says with a laugh.

But what turned the tide was when the re-rollout market worked at the ticket-window. “When the re-rollout of films that had tanked started doing well, I felt like I was onto something. Emraan also softened his stance on the market,” the filmmaker says.

title: 24 Years of Bend It Like Beckham: Gurinder Chadha’s film is the ONLY movie to have been distributed in every country, including North Korea; TV premiere was CENSORED by nearly 50 minutes
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bend It Like Beckham also achieved a rare distinction – it was screened in North Korea. During the promotions of her movie Christmas Karma (2025), Gurinder Chadha told Mid-Day's Mayank Shekhar, “ Bend It Like Beckham remains the only movie in the history of cinema to have been distributed in every country of the world, including North Korea!”

Adding to this, Bend It Like Beckham was first screened in North Korea at the 9th Pyongyang International Movie Festival in 2004. Festival organizer Nicholas Bonner wrote his first-hand account of the screening of the movie. He wrote, “If a movie is popular, it soon sells out. Which is exactly what happened with Bend It Like Beckham . The movie was a hit! It screened at 3 cinemas for 4 days and reached an audience of 12,000. An astonishing number in such a short time.”

Meanwhile, Then, on December 26, 2010, the movie made history by airing nationwide on North Korean state television (Korean Central Television). Nick Bonner, the man behind Beijing-based Koryo Tours, shared, “This is the first Western movie broadcast throughout the whole of North Korea.”
Notably, The broadcast was negotiated by the British Embassy in Pyongyang, led by Ambassador Peter Hughes, to commemorate 10 years of diplomatic relations between the UK and the DPRK.

As per the latest buzz, However, as per reports, the 112-minute-long movie was heavily censored and trimmed to just an hour for its North Korean broadcast. As per an article in Mail & Guardian, “Although Bend It like Beckham is about a sport beloved among North Koreans, the movie also tackles taboo topics, including interracial relationships, homosexuality and religion.”

In further updates, Bend It Like Beckham is about a soccer-mad teenage girl in London who revolts against her traditional Punjabi family by idolizing David Beckham and playing football in a local all-female team. It also starred Parminder Nagra, Anupam Kher, Zohra Sehgal and others.
